newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Huhtamaki ramps up on U.S. deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Huhtamaki ramps up on U.S. deal.

text.p: Shares in Finnish confectionery and packaging group Huhtamaki Oy surged to a record high on Friday as it sealed a deal with Hershey Foods which would clear its problems in the U.S. and sharpen its focus on growth areas.

The companies have reached preliminary agreement to take over each other's relatively low-yielding American and European operations, but Huhtamaki will retain its big U.S. brand names and on which Hershey will pay royalties, Huhtamaki said.
"This will have a significant positive impact on our profitability next year," Huhtamaki CEO Timo Peltola told a news conference.

News of the deal, within the last hour of official Helsinki trade, sparked frantic buying in the stock which marched up 33.00 markka ($7.15) or nearly 18 percent to 218.00 markka, its highest in at least five years.
In the U.S., Huhtamaki's main brands are Jolly Rancher, Whoppers, Good&Plenty and PayDay: it is better known in Europe for Chewits, Sportlife chewing gum and Elizabeth Shaw chocolates.
Hershey, best-known for the popular brand chocolate bar in the U.S., owns German praline maker Gubor Schokoladen and Italian sugar confectionery company Sperlari.

Huhtamaki, whose stock only recently started to outperform the Helsinki bourse, has recently been dogged by lower sales of its U.S. brands and its efforts to restructure Leaf have met stiff resistance.
It said in a statement the deal had been motivated by shareholder interest, allowing it to concentrate on building Leaf's growing European and Asian businesses.

The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, will involve Hershey paying $440 million for Huhtamaki's North American confectionery operations and Huhtamaki will pay $110 million for Hershey's European confectionery interests.
Leaf's North American confectionery net sales in 1995 were about $460 million, while Gubor and Sperlari had combined sales of about $210 million, Huhtamaki said.

Due to be completed by year-end, Huhtamaki said the deal meant it would retain ownership of Leaf's North American trademarks and receive an annual royalty on Hershey's sales of these brands. It declined to elaborate on the royalty.
Huhtamaki said Hershey had also suffered from lower profitability in Europe than in the United States.

"We will get new resources to develop the company in Europe and in Asia," Peltola said, adding that it would pick up about 1.5 billion markka to grow the company in a programme which would certainly include acquisitions.
"In my opinion, this is extremely good news," said one analyst, requesting anonymity. "They will get rid of the problems they've had in the U.S."

Huhtamaki's annual net sales -- 7.84 billion markka in 1995 -- will drop by about one billion markka after the deal, Peltola said. The company last week reported a 42 percent increase in January-August profit to 286 million markka. ($ = 4.609 Finnish Markka)
